Export an Equation List to SBML

Source: R/SBMLinterface.R
exportSbml.Rd

Writes an eqnlist with parameter values and initial values to an SBML Level 3 Version 2 file. Kinetic laws are multiplied by the volume of their compartment. Symbolic volumes are written as an <initialAssignment> of the compartment. Requires the same Python environment as importSbml().

Usage

exportSbml(
  eqnlist,
  parameters = NULL,
  inits = NULL,
  filepath,
  modelID = "dMod_export",
  events = NULL
)

Arguments

eqnlist

Object of class eqnlist to export.

parameters

Named numeric vector of parameter values (including any compartment-size parameters referenced in eqnlist$compartments). An entry named like a compartment whose volume is the compartment symbol is the size of that compartment; entries named like other compartments or like species are not written. Default NULL: no <parameter> is written.

inits

Named numeric or character vector of initial values keyed by state name. Numbers, also as character, are written as initialConcentration, or initialAmount for the states in eqnlist$amountStates; other expressions as <initialAssignment> formulas. Missing states default to 0. Default NULL.

filepath

Path of the SBML file to write.

modelID

SBML model identifier. Defaults to "dMod_export".

events

Object of class eventlist to emit as <listOfEvents>, or NULL. Rows sharing a trigger become one <event>. A root event becomes two events with the triggers root >= 0 and root <= 0, initially true, so that the SBML model fires at crossings in both directions and not at the start, as cppDE does. A compartment an event assigns to is written as non-constant. Default NULL.

Value

filepath, invisibly.

See also

importSbml(), exportPEtab()

Examples

f <- addReaction(eqnlist(), from = "A", to = "B", rate = "k1*A")
f <- addReaction(f, from = "B", to = "", rate = "k2*B")
file <- file.path(tempdir(), "model.xml")
exportSbml(f, parameters = c(k1 = 0.5, k2 = 0.1), inits = c(A = 1, B = 0),
           filepath = file)
model <- importSbml(file)
model$reactions
#> 
#>   Check Educt -> Product       Rate Description
#> 1           A ->       B 1 * k1 * A           1
#> 2           B ->         1 * k2 * B           2
model$pars
#>          k1          k2 defaultComp 
#>         0.5         0.1         1.0
